why: analyzeMissingIndexes() (src/db/queries.ts) only runs regex pattern-matching over the sql string to suggest CREATE INDEX statements; it never calls executeQuery or touches the database, so there is no execution/injection sink.

sink: assertSqlOperationAllowed() classifies the query only by its leading keyword; the sql is then run via executeQuery()/db.query() once per iteration (iterations is caller-controlled with no schema max)
guard: bypassable: sql="EXECUTE PROCEDURE <writing-procedure>" — assertSqlOperationAllowed() and checkAllowedOperation('EXECUTE') always allow the EXECUTE keyword by default, so a stored procedure that performs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL internally runs (repeatedly, `iterations` times) without ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true
why: This tool exists to benchmark a query by executing it multiple times, and it reuses the same assertSqlOperationAllowed()/checkAllowedOperation() gate as execute-query. Because that gate only inspects the SQL's leading keyword, EXECUTE PROCEDURE calls are always permitted and can trigger arbitrary writes inside the called procedure, repeated `iterations` times (no upper bound in the Zod schema). Exploitability depends on a writable stored procedure already existing in the target database, which this static review cannot confirm.
contract: SQL operation ${normalizedOperation} is disabled by default. Set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true to enable trusted raw writes.

sink: each query.sql in the caller-supplied batch (up to 20 queries, 10-way concurrency) is checked with assertSqlOperationAllowed() then executed via executeBatchQueries()->executeQuery()->db.query()
guard: bypassable: queries=[{sql:"EXECUTE PROCEDURE <writing-procedure>"}] — identical bypass to execute-query, applied independently to every item in the batch
why: Same root cause as execute-query: assertSqlOperationAllowed() treats EXECUTE as always-permitted regardless of what the called procedure does internally, so a batch entry can invoke a stored procedure that performs writes/DDL without ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true. This requires a writable procedure to already exist in the target database, which cannot be confirmed statically.
contract: SQL operation ${normalizedOperation} is disabled by default. Set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true to enable trusted raw writes.

sink: assertSqlOperationAllowed(sql) classifies the query only by its leading keyword via getSqlOperation(); when that keyword is EXECUTE, checkAllowedOperation('EXECUTE') is checked against the default allowedOperations=['SELECT','EXECUTE'] and always passes, then executeQuery()->db.query() runs it
guard: bypassable: sql="EXECUTE PROCEDURE <writing-procedure>" — the write-protection gate (which requires ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/etc.) only inspects the SQL's leading keyword, so wrapping a write inside any stored procedure and invoking it via EXECUTE PROCEDURE sails through the gate untouched
why: execute-query accepts a fully caller-controlled sql string. Once assertSqlOperationAllowed() and checkAllowedOperation() pass, it is sent verbatim to the Firebird driver. Both checks treat the literal keyword EXECUTE as always-allowed by default, so calling any stored procedure that itself performs writes/DDL bypasses the tool's own stated write-protection ('disabled by default, set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true'). Whether this is exploitable in a given deployment depends on a writable stored procedure already existing in that Firebird database, which this static review cannot confirm — hence Tier B rather than A.
contract: SQL operation ${normalizedOperation} is disabled by default. Set ALLOW_RAW_SQL=true to enable trusted raw writes.

why: get-database-info takes no arguments and only calls listTables(), a static parameter-less SQL query; there is no caller-controlled input at all.

getExecutionPlan() (src/db/queries.ts) validates the sql and requires it to start with SELECT, but never actually executes the query or calls any DB driver method — it returns a static explanatory message because node-firebird/node-firebird-driver-native do not expose a plan API. There is no execution sink.
tableName is checked with validateSql() and then bound as a `?` parameter in getFieldDescriptions() (src/db/queries.ts) rather than being concatenated into the SQL text.
get-server-info takes no arguments and only reads package.json/process metadata; no caller-controlled input reaches any sink.

checkAllowedOperation('SELECT') is enforced, tableName/column names are only usable if they pass quoteIdentifier()'s allow-listed regex (^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$), and all filter/order values are always bound as `?` parameters, never concatenated.
toolName is only used as a Map lookup key against the in-process tool registry; it never reaches a file, command, or SQL sink.
listAvailableEvents() runs a fixed, parameter-less SQL string with no caller-controlled input.
the optional `category` argument only filters an in-memory array of already-registered tool metadata; it never reaches a file, command, or SQL sink.
listFunctions() runs a fixed, parameter-less SQL string with no caller-controlled input.
listPackages() runs a fixed, parameter-less SQL string with no caller-controlled input.
listProcedures() runs a fixed, parameter-less SQL string with no caller-controlled input.
listTables() runs a fixed, parameter-less SQL string with no caller-controlled input.
listTriggers() runs a fixed, parameter-less SQL string with no caller-controlled input.

eventName is passed to registerFirebirdEvents()->attachment.queueEvents(), the Firebird native driver's dedicated event-registration API (isc_que_events wire protocol), not to a SQL string; it is only ever used as an event-name key, never interpreted as SQL, a path, or a command.
system-health-check takes no arguments and only reports process/memory metadata; no caller-controlled input reaches any sink.
verify-wire-encryption takes no arguments and only reads process.env flags (USE_NATIVE_DRIVER, WIRE_CRYPT); no caller-controlled input is involved.
each tableName is checked with validateSql() and then passed into describeTable(), which binds it as a `?` parameter (src/db/queries.ts) rather than interpolating it into SQL text.
functionName is checked with validateSql() and then bound as a `?` parameter in the RDB$FUNCTIONS query (src/db/metadata.ts); no string concatenation into SQL.
packageName is checked with validateSql() and then bound as a `?` parameter in the RDB$PACKAGES query (src/db/metadata.ts); no string concatenation into SQL.
procedureName is checked with validateSql() and then bound as a `?` parameter in the RDB$PROCEDURES query (src/db/metadata.ts); no string concatenation into SQL.
tableName passes checkAllowedTable() and validateSql(), and is bound as a `?` parameter in describeTable() (src/db/queries.ts) rather than interpolated into SQL text.
triggerName is checked with validateSql() and then bound as a `?` parameter in the RDB$TRIGGERS query (src/db/metadata.ts); no string concatenation into SQL.
echo (src/tools/simple.ts) returns args.message verbatim as text content; it is never opened, executed, or interpreted by anything.
checkAllowedOperation('SELECT') and checkAllowedTable() are enforced, and tableName can only reach the query text after passing quoteIdentifier()'s allow-listed identifier regex.
addMultipleReactionsHandler forwards each caller-supplied emoji string straight to discord.js message.react(); the only effect is reacting on messages the bot's own token can already access.
addReactionHandler forwards the caller-supplied emoji straight to discord.js message.react(); the sink is the bot's own Discord account/resources.

assignRoleHandler forwards guildId/userId/roleId to discord.js member.roles.add(); Discord's own role-hierarchy permission model (a bot cannot grant a role at or above its own highest role) is the effective control here, not application code, and this is exactly the tool's declared purpose.
createCategoryHandler forwards name/position/reason to discord.js guild.channels.create(); no injection surface, plain API forwarding.
createForumChannelHandler forwards name/topic/categoryId/reason to discord.js guild.channels.create(); plain API forwarding.

createForumPostHandler forwards title/content/tags to discord.js forumChannel.threads.create(); tags are matched against the forum's own availableTags list, so arbitrary strings cannot select unintended tags.

createRoleHandler resolves permission name strings only through PermissionsBitField.Flags (unknown names are silently skipped) and forwards to guild.roles.create(); granting broad permissions to a new role is exactly the tool's declared purpose and is bounded by the bot's own Discord permissions.
createTextChannelHandler forwards channelName/topic/categoryId/reason to discord.js guild.channels.create(); plain API forwarding.
createVoiceChannelHandler forwards channelName/categoryId/userLimit/reason to discord.js guild.channels.create(); plain API forwarding.

sink: channel.createWebhook({avatar}) -> discord.js GuildChannelManager.createWebhook() -> DataResolver.resolveImage(avatar) -> resolveFile(): any string starting with 'http(s)://' is fetch()'ed server-side, and any other non-'data:' string is treated as a local filesystem path and read with fs.readFile()
dep_evidence: node_modules/discord.js@14.26.5 src/util/DataResolver.js lines 83-106 (resolveFile) and src/managers/GuildChannelManager.js line 234 (resolvedImage = await resolveImage(avatar)) — resolveImage/resolveFile apply no scheme or host allow-list before fetching or reading from disk; the library's own JSDoc for BufferResolvable warns 'discord.js will fetch the URL internally in order to create a Buffer. This can pose a security risk when the URL has not been sanitized'
why: The `avatar` argument (a bare z.string(), no format restriction) flows unchanged from the MCP tool args into discord.js's createWebhook call, which resolves it via resolveImage->resolveFile. A URL such as an internal cloud-metadata address is fetched by the MCP server process itself (SSRF), and any value that is not an http(s) URL or a data: URI is instead resolved with path.resolve() and read from the local filesystem via fs.readFile, uploading that file's bytes to Discord as the webhook avatar — an arbitrary local file read/exfiltration primitive. Neither the schema nor the handler validates or restricts the value at all.
contract: Optional avatar URL or data for the webhook.

why: deleteCategoryHandler forwards categoryId/reason to discord.js category.delete(); plain API forwarding on a resource the bot already has access to.
deleteChannelHandler forwards channelId/reason to discord.js channel.delete(); plain API forwarding.
deleteForumPostHandler forwards threadId/reason to discord.js thread.delete(); plain API forwarding.
deleteMessageHandler forwards channelId/messageId to discord.js message.delete(); plain API forwarding.
deleteRoleHandler forwards guildId/roleId/reason to discord.js role.delete(); plain API forwarding, bounded by Discord's own role hierarchy.
deleteWebhookHandler uses the caller-supplied webhookId/webhookToken purely as webhook credentials to call discord.js webhook.delete(); no local resolution of the token value happens (unlike avatar).
editCategoryHandler forwards name/position/reason to discord.js category.edit(); plain API forwarding.
editChannelHandler forwards name/topic/parentId/position/reason to discord.js channel.edit(); plain API forwarding.
editMessageHandler explicitly checks message.author.id !== client.user?.id and refuses to edit any message not authored by the bot itself, in addition to being a plain API forward otherwise.
editRoleHandler forwards name/color/hoist/mentionable/permissions/position/reason to discord.js role.edit(); plain API forwarding, bounded by Discord's own role hierarchy.

sink: webhook.edit({avatar}) -> discord.js Webhook.edit(): 'if (avatar && !avatar.startsWith("data:")) avatar = await resolveImage(avatar)' -> resolveFile(): fetch()'s http(s) URLs server-side, or fs.readFile()'s any other string as a local path
dep_evidence: node_modules/discord.js@14.26.5 src/structures/Webhook.js lines 282-284 (edit(): avatar = await resolveImage(avatar) unless it already starts with 'data:') and src/util/DataResolver.js resolveFile() (lines 83-106) — identical unguarded resolveImage/resolveFile path as createWebhook
why: Same mechanism as discord_create_webhook: the caller-controlled `avatar` string is passed to discord.js Webhook.edit(), which calls resolveImage/resolveFile whenever the value doesn't already start with 'data:'. An http(s) URL is fetched by the server process (SSRF, including to internal-only hosts), and any other non-data string is read from the local filesystem via fs.readFile and re-uploaded to Discord as the webhook's avatar, giving arbitrary local file disclosure. No validation exists in the schema or handler.
getForumChannelsHandler only lists forum channels in a guild via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
getForumPostHandler only fetches thread details/messages via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
getForumTagsHandler only lists a forum channel's availableTags via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
getMemberHandler only fetches and formats member info via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
getReactionUsersHandler only fetches the users who reacted to a message via discord.js REST reads; read-only, no injection surface.
getServerInfoHandler only fetches and formats guild/channel info via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
listForumThreadsHandler only lists active/archived threads via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
listMembersHandler only lists guild members via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
listPinnedMessagesHandler only lists pinned messages via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
listRolesHandler only lists guild roles via discord.js reads; read-only, no injection surface.
listServersHandler takes no arguments and only lists guilds the bot is a member of; read-only, no caller-controlled input.

the optional `token` argument is used exactly as documented by its own schema ("the bot token to use for login") to call discord.js client.login(); allowing the caller to choose which bot account the server authenticates as is the tool's stated purpose, not a bypass of any separate control.
pinMessageHandler forwards channelId/messageId/reason to discord.js message.pin(); plain API forwarding.

readMessagesHandler only fetches messages via discord.js channel.messages.fetch(); before/after/around are validated by resolveSnowflakeOrDate() (must be a 17-20 digit snowflake or a parseable date) before use. Read-only, no injection surface.
removeChannelPermissionsHandler forwards channelId/roleId/reason to discord.js channel.permissionOverwrites.delete(); plain API forwarding.
removeReactionHandler forwards channelId/messageId/emoji/userId to discord.js reaction.users.remove(); plain API forwarding.
removeRoleHandler forwards guildId/userId/roleId/reason to discord.js member.roles.remove(); plain API forwarding, bounded by Discord's own role hierarchy.
replyToForumHandler forwards message content to discord.js thread.send(); plain API forwarding, no local resolution of the string.

sink: guildId is template-interpolated unescaped directly into the REST request path passed to context.client.rest.get(); every other filter (content, authorId, channelId, etc.) is instead appended through URLSearchParams.append(), which percent-encodes its values
guard: partial: the Zod schema only requires guildId to be a non-empty string (min(1)); there is no digits-only/snowflake format check and no encodeURIComponent() call before the value is placed in the URL path, so characters such as '/', '..' or '?' in guildId are forwarded verbatim into the request path
why: Unlike the query-string filters, guildId is not passed through URLSearchParams and is not validated as a snowflake, so it reaches the REST path unescaped. A guildId value containing path-altering characters (e.g. '/', '..') could change which endpoint or query is actually requested with the bot's own authorization, beyond the intended guild-message-search route. I could not confirm from static reading how undici/Discord's servers would normalize such a path, so I can't fully prove the resulting endpoint-redirection outcome — hence Tier B, not A.
contract: Search messages in a server with various filters.

why: sendMessageHandler forwards message content to discord.js channel.send(); plain API forwarding, no local resolution of the string.

sendWebhookMessageHandler forwards content/username/avatarURL to discord.js webhook.send(); avatarURL here is bundled as-is into the JSON body sent to Discord's webhook-execute endpoint (verified in node_modules/discord.js structures/Webhook.js send(), which never calls resolveImage/resolveFile for this path) — Discord's own servers, not the MCP process, would fetch it, so there is no local SSRF/file-read as there is for create/edit webhook's `avatar` field.
setChannelPermissionsHandler resolves permission name strings only through PermissionsBitField.Flags and forwards to discord.js channel.permissionOverwrites.edit(); plain API forwarding.
setForumTagsHandler forwards tag name/emoji/moderated fields to discord.js forumChannel.setAvailableTags(); plain API forwarding.
unpinMessageHandler forwards channelId/messageId/reason to discord.js message.unpin(); plain API forwarding.

updateForumPostHandler forwards name/archived/locked to discord.js thread.edit(), and resolves `tags` only against the parent forum's own availableTags (by name or ID) before applying; plain API forwarding with no unvalidated pass-through.
